title: Contract & deployment gateways alignment
summary: Redwood AE/SE walked Pioneer Payments through MSA/DPA redline approach and technical preflight for a Private deployment pilot. Key concerns: EU data residency, KMS integration (customer-managed key), egress costs, SLA credits, and indemnity language. Agreed next steps include sending a tailored security packet, revised pricing for a 3-month pilot, and a technical runbook for VPC peering and canary routing.

Ethan to provide VPC peering runbook and sample terraform by 2025-03-07
Pioneer to share MSA redlines and DPA exceptions (Nina) by 2025-03-05
Schedule pilot kick-off (pilot PO) after redline triage - target week of 2025-03-17

Ethan: Draft VPC peering + terraform example, include KMS flow - due 2025-03-07

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-01 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Priya (CSM), Laura (Pioneer Head of Platform), Diego (Procurement), Nina (Legal), Tom (SRE), Anya (Product)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone thanks for joining, can you hear me okay?
[00:06] Laura: Yep loud and clear, thanks.
[00:10] Maya: Cool. Quick agenda — legal redlines, security posture, and then Ethan will do a deployment preflight on VPC/KMS and we close with pricing for the pilot. Sound good?
[00:22] Diego: Yep that's it from procurement side.
[00:25] Nina: Fine. We'll try to keep it tight.
[00:30] Maya: Great. Nina, do you want to kick off with the MSA/DPA hotspots you flagged?
[00:35] Nina: Sure. We did a pass and main items are indemnity cap language, data residency clause for EU customer data, and a couple DPA bits around subprocessors and audit rights. Also curious about egress fee visibility in the pricing.
[00:50] Maya: Understood. For indemnity and cap, we typically start with our standard MSA language but we can discuss a carve for regulated data. We do have an enterprise addendum path—I've flagged it in the notes and will circulate an annotated version.
[01:05] Tom: Is there a standard SLA? Last time we saw tiered SLAs but need clarity what happens during large model fallbacks, like where Redwood routes to lower-cost models and what the SLO seren.. sorry SLO and credits look like.
[01:20] Ethan: Yeah good question. We have per-route latency SLOs and an SLA credit table in the enterprise docs. Practically, we offer canary rollouts and automatic fallback to compatible model variants; the SLA covers latency when serving pinned models. If fallback to a lower tier happens because of capacity, that's handled by the routing policy — credits apply when request success rate drops below X and latency exceeds configured p95.
[01:45] Laura: So is that a break-glass scenario? If we push a big batch overnight and intercept happens, are we on the hook for retries?
[01:55] Ethan: We recommend client-side retry/backoff; platform will surface a header when fallback occurs so you can count it. We also support prefix/KV caching to reduce replays. I'll include header examples in the runbook.
[02:10] Anya: For our product team it's important that model behavior is stable. How do we handle model version pinning vs updates?
[02:18] Maya: You can pin a model version per route, and rollouts support canary/A-B and automatic fallback. Redwood Optimize will also suggest quantization or model variants if latency/cost tradeoff arises, but we won't silently swap your pinned version.
[02:35] Nina: On DPA — subprocessors list? We have a procurement rule that requires 30-day notice for adding subprocessors and a right to audit.
[02:45] Maya: We publish a subprocessors list and give notice periods in the DPA. For on-prem/private deployments, you can choose a private control plane or an on-prem package to eliminate subprocessors. That might be relevant for EU data residency.
[03:00] Nina: Hmm. We need KMS integration with our HSM — customer-managed keys. Any gotchas?
[03:08] Ethan: We support bring-your-own-key via standard KMS integrations; we can walk through both cloud KMS (Cloud KMS / AWS KMS) and an HSM key wrapping flow. For Private deployments, the key material never leaves your HSM; we use KMS-encrypted secrets for bootstrap. I'll show the flow in the runbook.
[03:28] Tom: Network-wise, VPC peering vs private link? We need a path with stable egress characteristics and predictable throughput.
[03:36] Ethan: We support VPC peering in our Private offering and transit gateway setups. For Hosted, we offer PrivateLink for AWS. We also have Burst capacity for Dedicated pools if you need predictable throughput. I'll include example terraform and bandwidth guidance.
[03:55] Diego: Let's talk pricing. We need a short pilot — three months ideally — with predictable cost and a pilot PO. How does commit and overage work?
[04:05] Maya: For pilot we can offer a committed monthly spend with a blended unit price. If you exceed committed capacity we bill at an overage rate. We can include trial credits upfront and a PO for the pilot period. We'll send a pricing sheet with two scenarios: 3-month pilot and 12-month reserved.
[04:20] Nina: On the MSA, we have a hard stop around export controls and data export. We need to ensure EU data stays in-region.
[04:27] Ethan: We have region-based routing and can pin serving to EU regions; for Private you can deploy into a customer VPC in eu-west-1 or our partner region. The data-routing policy can be configured in the deployment manifest.
[04:45] Laura: Operational question — how do we get logs and traces? We want token-level cost breakdowns and per-route latency traces.
[04:53] Priya: Redwood Console exposes token-level cost and latency breakdown. For Private we can stream logs into your SIEM via a forwarder; or you can pull logs via our API. We also have tracing hooks you can plug into Jaeger/Datadog.
[05:10] Tom: Is there PII redaction support at inference? We occasionally need to drop PHI before sending to model.
[05:16] Ethan: We have pre-send hooks you can run in a managed preprocessor layer. For private deployments you can enforce it on-prem. We'll include a doc for redaction patterns.
[05:30] Nina: Back to legal — indemnity caps and liability. We're pushing to limit open-ended liability for model hallucinations; can Redwood accept language that ties liability to negligence or willful misconduct?
[05:45] Maya: Our standard is capped liability with carve-outs for gross negligence. We can propose a mutual limitation; I'll work with legal to produce a compromise redline.
[05:55] Diego: Procurement needs to know escrow and termination windows. If we terminate mid-quarter how are refunds handled?
[06:03] Maya: We can pro-rate and outline termination with 30 days' notice. For reserved capacity there are typically commit windows; pilot will be simpler — pro rata refunds for unused committed spend if termination occurs within agreed early termination terms.
[06:20] Anya: For the pilot success criteria we'll measure P95 latency < 300ms for the 512 token median prompt, 99.9% availability for inference endpoints, and a cost per request threshold.
[06:32] Priya: Noted — we'll capture those metrics as pilot acceptance criteria.
[06:35] Nina: Are there standard SOC 2 artifacts? We need the report and the pen-test summary.
[06:41] Maya: Yes — SOC2 Type II, ISO27001 summary, and a redacted pen-test report. I'll attach the security pack.
[06:50] Laura: On the deployment timeline, if we sign the pilot PO mid-March when can we expect an environment?
[06:57] Ethan: For Private VPC peering pilot we typically need 2-3 weeks for networking and keying once PO and access info are provided. If you choose Dedicated reserved capacity it's about 1-2 weeks. We'll put together a timeline in the runbook.
[07:12] Tom: Can we run a short performance benchmark as part of pilot? We want to validate token throughput at our 99th percentile message size.
[07:20] Ethan: Absolutely — we'll run a POC benchmark with your workload profile. We ask you to provide representative prompts and expected RPS.
[07:30] Diego: Regarding subprocessors the one big ask from procurement: ability to terminate if certain subprocessors change.
[07:38] Maya: For hosted models we have subprocessors; for Private you can minimize subprocessors. We'll document both options and the notice period.
[07:50] Nina: A small item — data retention and logs. We need logs retained for 6 months and the ability to extract them for audits.
[07:58] Priya: We can set retention; for Private you control retention locally. For Hosted, enterprise plans allow configurable retention windows and export APIs.
[08:10] Anya: One more product note, we need function calling / tool calls in a secure way. Does Redwood support signing or verification of tool outputs?
[08:19] Ethan: We support structured outputs and can sign responses using your key if needed in Private deployments. For Hosted we have an option to HMAC responses. I'll include both flows.
[08:35] Laura: Great. Let's talk concrete redline exchange cadence. We want to drop annotated MSA back by Wednesday.
[08:42] Nina: Yes that's the plan — we'll send by 2025-03-05.
[08:46] Maya: Perfect. We'll circulate our suggested compromise redlines and the security pack by 2025-03-04.
[08:52] Diego: For procurement approvals we usually need a 3-week window once legal signs off. Can we compress that if pilot PO is small?
[08:59] Maya: We can work with finance to expedite for pilot POs under threshold; I'll note that and loop finance if needed.
[09:08] Tom: For the technical runbook — include expected port/IP ranges, TLS ciphers, cert pinning options, and example iptables rules.
[09:18] Ethan: Will do. Also sample terraform for VPC peering and a small k8s helm chart for the edge connector.
[09:28] Laura: Thanks. Anything else?
[09:31] Maya: Quick recap then close. Action items: Maya sends security packet and pricing; Ethan sends VPC/KMS runbook and benchmark plan; Pioneer sends annotated MSA/DPA; Tom sends SRE latency profile. We'll target a pilot kickoff week of 2025-03-17 pending redline resolution.
[09:52] Diego: Sounds good.
[09:54] Nina: Thanks everyone.
[10:00] Maya: Thanks all, we'll follow up in email with links.

Notes (links shared in chat): security-pack.pdf, pricing-sheet.csv, vpc-runbook-draft.md, sample-terraform.zip, msa-annotated-request.pdf

Transcript notes: transcription contains occasional errors (product names sometimes split, e.g., Redwood pry-vate), speaker interruptions and overlapped talk.
additional_notes: Pilot acceptance criteria drafted during call; pricing scenarios to be sent. Legal will send annotated MSA/DPA. Redwood to provide security artifacts and technical runbook.
